column1: # Words Odia speakers routinely write in Odia script but which are NOT
# phonetically derivable from the Odia phonetic rules: English spelling says
# little about English sound, so "school" would come out ସ୍ଚୂଲ and "phone"
# ଫୋନେ. Typed on the Odia phonetic layout, the English spelling on the left
# resolves directly to the Odia form on the right, ahead of the rules and of
# Spellings follow the bundled Odia word list: where it writes both a bare
# final consonant (ଫୋନ) and one with an explicit halant (ମ୍ୟାଚ୍), the commoner
# form is used. Words Odia prefers to translate (book ବହି, airport
# ବିମାନବନ୍ଦର) are left out on purpose.
# A hand-written draft that wants an Odia speaker's review. A wrong entry here
# is worse than a missing one, since it outranks everything.
# Format: english<TAB>odia   (one mapping per line; # starts a comment)
# Keep the English key lowercase. First column is matched case-insensitively.
